title: Build up to the target's length
statement: Build practice up to the length and load of the performance it prepares for, because mastering short pieces one at a time does not build sustained work.
example: One course's passages ran 58 to 217 words, while the test it prepared for presents up to roughly 2,740 words.
detail: A course review found a Grade 3 course's passages ran 58 to 217 words, while the state test it prepares for presents up to roughly 2,740 words across two single passages and one paired set, so a child could master the whole course one short snippet at a time and never sustain attention across a multi-passage block (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5_build_2026_07_02/feedback_clean.md`). It asked for longer passages and paired-text sets that build toward test length and real-world reading.
against: This is a review's judgment; nothing in these sources measured stamina.

evidence.quote: A child can master the whole course one short snippet at a time and never once sustain attention across a multi-passage block.
***To change this:*** Add longer passages and paired-text sets that build toward test-length and real-world reading.
